project.name: tetrouge
project.description: A Tetris roguelite game built in Godot 4 (GDScript) where players fight enemies by playing Tetris and collecting roguelite upgrades (technique cards, keystones, consumables).

nodes.name: ascension_manager.gd
nodes.summary: Autoload singleton that tracks the player's ascension (New Game+) level and provides cumulative difficulty modifier dictionaries for each level from 0 (base game) up to 6.
nodes.languageNotes: GDScript autoload — registered as AscensionManager in project.godot, globally accessible to all scenes.

nodes.name: get_modifiers
nodes.summary: Returns the cumulative modifier dictionary for the given ascension level, clamped to the valid range.

nodes.name: economy.gd
nodes.summary: Autoload singleton managing the player's coin economy, including adding/spending coins, checking affordability, applying interest, and emitting a coins_changed signal for UI updates.
nodes.languageNotes: Emits coins_changed signal on every mutation, letting HUD and shop UI reactively update without polling.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Resets coin balance and interest cap to defaults and emits the coins_changed signal.

nodes.name: apply_interest
nodes.summary: Calculates interest as coins/5 capped by interest_cap, adds it to the coin total, and returns the interest earned.

nodes.name: resource_registry.gd
nodes.summary: Autoload singleton acting as the central asset registry — statically preloads all keystones, techniques, consumables, vouchers, and enemies so they are available across web and desktop exports without runtime filesystem scanning.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses compile-time preload() instead of DirAccess.open() specifically to support Godot web exports where the PCK virtual filesystem makes runtime directory scanning unavailable.

nodes.name: find_by_id
nodes.summary: Static linear search through any resource collection by id string, returning the matching Resource or null.

nodes.name: get_available_keystones
nodes.summary: Returns all keystones from the registry filtered to those whose unlock_condition_id is empty or already in the player's ProfileSave unlocked IDs.

nodes.name: get_available_techniques
nodes.summary: Returns all techniques from the registry filtered to those whose unlock_condition_id is empty or already in ProfileSave unlocked IDs.

nodes.name: export_presets.cfg
nodes.summary: Godot export configuration defining Windows Desktop (x86_64) and Web (HTML5) build presets, both excluding GUT test files, targeting ../builds/ output paths, and setting the product name to Tetrouge.
nodes.languageNotes: Web preset disables thread support (variant/thread_support=false) which is required for Godot web exports on browsers without SharedArrayBuffer isolation.

nodes.name: attack_context.gd
nodes.summary: Data class (Resource) carrying all contextual information about a single Tetris placement event, including lines cleared, combo count, T-spin type, back-to-back state, board height, and placement metadata used by techniques to compute damage.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses @export on every field so instances can be configured in the Godot editor and inspected at runtime.

nodes.name: boss_modifier.gd
nodes.summary: Resource class defining a boss modifier, which applies difficulty-altering flags (disable hold, hide previews, time limit, narrow board, random pieces, garbage rules, quota whitelist) to a RoundConfig when a boss round starts.
nodes.languageNotes: apply_to_config() uses a conditional-field pattern — only non-default values overwrite the config, preserving base settings for modifiers that don't specify a given field.

nodes.name: apply_to_config
nodes.summary: Writes non-default modifier fields onto a RoundConfig object to apply the boss's rule changes before the round begins.

nodes.name: attack_counts_toward_quota
nodes.summary: Returns true if the given attack event type is permitted to contribute to the boss quota, based on whether the whitelist is empty or contains the type.

nodes.name: consumable.gd
nodes.summary: Resource class defining a single-use consumable item with timing, cost, and flat attack bonus fields that are applied to a RoundConfig when the consumable is activated.
nodes.languageNotes: UseTiming enum distinguishes between round-start pre-application, mid-round usage, and anytime usage, controlling when the item may be activated.

nodes.name: apply_to_config
nodes.summary: Applies this consumable's bonus fields to the given RoundConfig, incrementing attack bonus accumulators and surge clear counters.

nodes.name: the_ancient.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Ancient' — sets random_pieces=true, causing all Tetris pieces to be drawn in random order rather than from the standard bag.

nodes.name: the_blitz.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Blitz' — overrides the round time limit to 120 seconds, forcing the player to defeat the enemy within 2 minutes or end their run.

nodes.name: the_fateless.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Fateless' — sets hide_all_previews=true, hiding the piece queue and next piece from the player.

nodes.name: the_filth.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Filth' — sets garbage_individual_lines=true, causing all incoming garbage to arrive as separate single lines instead of bursts.

nodes.name: the_purge.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Aristocrat' — restricts quota_whitelist to quads, T-spins, and perfect clears, meaning only those attack types contribute to the boss's HP.

nodes.name: the_reflection.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Reflection' — sets reflect_ratio=0.5, causing half of every attack that damages the boss to be reflected back as garbage to the player.

nodes.name: the_silencer.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Silent' — sets disable_b2b=true, preventing back-to-back chains from forming during the boss round.

nodes.name: the_thin.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Thin' — overrides board_width_override=8, narrowing the Tetris board from 10 to 8 columns for the boss round.

nodes.name: the_void.tres
nodes.summary: BossModifier data asset for 'The Void' — sets disable_hold=true, preventing the player from using the hold piece mechanic during the boss round.

nodes.name: power_fragment.tres

nodes.summary: Keystone resource granting a 3x damage multiplier on the first Perfect Clear each round, categorized under the PC technique group.

nodes.name: blessed_stone.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource providing a one-time board-top-out forgiveness: clears the board and grants 2 extra minutes, categorized as Utility.

nodes.name: consistency.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource adding +1 damage to every Back-to-Back clear, rewarding sustained B2B streaks.

nodes.name: crystal_staff.tres
nodes.summary: Upgraded Starter keystone that replaces Simple Wand and grants +10 damage on all T-Spins, forming a weapon upgrade chain.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses requires_keystone_id and replaces_keystone_id to implement a keystone upgrade chain pattern.

nodes.name: daze.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource that delays the next garbage drop by 2 seconds after each Quad clear, providing defensive utility in the Quad category.

nodes.name: dizzy.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource rewarding excessive T-piece rotation: if rotated more than 4 times before locking, the T-Spin deals +4 damage.

nodes.name: double_trouble.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource doubling the damage of T-Spin Doubles, focusing on the T-Spin technique category.

nodes.name: dual_wielding.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource that doubles damage for consecutive Quad clears, incentivizing chained Quad play.

nodes.name: enchant.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource that adds +2 damage to T-Spins for each T-Spin-applicable technique active, scaling with build complexity.

nodes.name: final_blow.tres
nodes.summary: High-risk B2B keystone that deals burst damage equal to 2x the streak length when B2B breaks, then permanently disables B2B.

nodes.name: flexible.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource making all spins preserve the B2B streak, broadening which moves maintain Back-to-Back continuity.

nodes.name: flurry.tres
nodes.summary: Keystone resource that doubles combo damage once the combo count exceeds 5, rewarding extended combo chains.

nodes.name: foresight.tres
nodes.summary: Utility keystone that adds 2 extra pieces to the preview queue, improving board planning and setup potential.

nodes.name: full_potential.tres
nodes.summary: Utility keystone granting instant auto-repeat, instant soft drop, and skipped line-clear delay for maximum piece movement speed.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets three boolean flags (instant_arr, instant_soft_drop, skip_line_clear_delay), making it one of the most mechanically impactful utility keystones.

nodes.name: golden_watch.tres
nodes.summary: Economic keystone granting a 3-minute bonus timer that converts remaining seconds into coins at round end (1 coin per 5 seconds).

nodes.name: great_sword.tres
nodes.summary: Upgraded Starter keystone replacing Simple Sword and granting +10 damage on Quads, part of the Quad weapon upgrade chain.

nodes.name: holy_cheese.tres
nodes.summary: Niche Combo keystone that doubles Singles damage while suppressing all other clear types, building around a Singles-only strategy.

nodes.name: hybrid_reactor.tres
nodes.summary: Utility keystone that grants +3 damage per attack for each technique carrying 2 or more tags, rewarding hybrid multi-tag builds.
nodes.languageNotes: Lacks script_class and uid fields compared to other keystones, suggesting it was added or edited outside the Godot editor at some point.

nodes.name: legionnaires_shield.tres
nodes.summary: Upgraded Starter keystone replacing Simple Shield and reducing incoming garbage by 3 lines per flush, forming the defensive upgrade chain.

nodes.name: mace_and_chain.tres
nodes.summary: Upgraded Starter keystone replacing Simple Flail and granting +3 damage to both Singles and Doubles, supporting a low-clear combo build.

nodes.name: magical_coin.tres
nodes.summary: Upgraded Economic keystone replacing Slightly Magical Coin and granting 4 extra coins at the end of each round.

nodes.name: midas_touch.tres
nodes.summary: Economic keystone that converts overkill damage into coins at round end, rewarding aggressive high-damage play.

nodes.summary: Utility keystone (internally named 'deflect') that reflects 50% of accepted garbage lines back as damage, turning defense into offense.

nodes.name: risky_business.tres
nodes.summary: Utility keystone that doubles damage for clears performed in the top 5 rows of the board, rewarding high-stack aggressive play.

nodes.name: safety_net.tres
nodes.summary: Godot Resource defining the 'Safety Net' keystone, which allows the player's B2B streak to be broken one extra time before resetting; categorized under 'B2B'.

nodes.name: sharpen.tres

nodes.name: simple_flail.tres

nodes.name: simple_shield.tres

nodes.name: slightly_magical_bag.tres
nodes.summary: Godot Resource defining the 'Bag of Holding' starter keystone (id: bag_of_holding), granting an extra hold slot with free swapping; a utility-focused starter.

nodes.name: slightly_magical_coin.tres
nodes.summary: Godot Resource defining the 'Slightly Magical Coin' starter keystone, earning 1 extra coin at the end of each round; an economy-focused starter for the shop upgrade path.

tour.title: Project Configuration
tour.description: The Godot project manifest is the ideal starting point: it declares the application name (Tetrouge v0.2.2), the main scene, every autoload singleton that makes up the global service layer, all input action bindings, and the display settings. Reading it gives you a complete map of what gets bootstrapped before any game code runs, and establishes the vocabulary of singleton names (Economy, RunState, ResourceRegistry, etc.) you will encounter throughout the rest of the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Godot autoloads are singletons registered in project.godot — they are instantiated once at startup and accessible globally by name from any script, replacing the need for manual service-locator patterns. The order they are listed determines initialization order.

tour.title: Resource Data Models
tour.description: Before any logic runs, the game defines its domain objects as GDScript Resource subclasses. Technique, Keystone, Enemy, RoundConfig, Consumable, Voucher, and BossModifier are the six core data types — each is a schema-like class with exported fields that get populated by .tres asset files at runtime. Understanding these classes first means every reference to 'a Technique' or 'a Keystone' in later scripts will be immediately legible.
tour.languageLesson: In Godot 4, extending Resource gives a class file-based serialization for free. The @export annotation makes a field visible in the inspector and included in .tres files. This pattern is how all game-design data (damage numbers, names, tags) is kept out of code and inside editable asset files.

tour.title: Attack Context & Combat Data Flow
tour.description: AttackContext and TechniqueRoundState are the two data-transfer objects that flow through the combat pipeline on every piece placement. AttackContext is a snapshot of one Tetris event (lines cleared, combo, T-spin type, B2B state, board height), while TechniqueRoundState tracks cumulative per-round counters (how many placements, clears, and one-shot flags). These two classes define the information contract between TetrisBoard, TechniqueEvaluator, and RunManager.

tour.title: Data Asset Catalogues
tour.description: The ResourceRegistry autoload preloads every .tres file — all technique cards, keystones, enemies, consumables, and vouchers — into in-memory arrays at startup. This is the project's answer to dynamic asset loading being unreliable in web exports: a single central registry ensures all content is available without filesystem scanning. The registry exposes filter methods (get_available_keystones, get_available_techniques) that RunManager and the Shop call to build the player's choices.
tour.languageLesson: Godot's preload() resolves a path at script compile time and embeds the resource reference. load() defers until runtime. Using preload() in an autoload guarantees assets are ready before any scene requests them, which is critical for web builds where the virtual filesystem behaves differently from desktop.

tour.title: Global Run State
tour.description: RunState is the single source of truth for everything that persists during an active roguelite run: the player's current stage and round, their full inventory of keystones, techniques, consumables, and vouchers, the seeded RNG instance, and the quota/time-limit calculations for each round. Nearly every other system reads from or writes to RunState, making it the hub of the architecture. The advance_round and reset methods bookend each combat encounter.

tour.title: Economy & Ascension Services
tour.description: Economy is a small focused autoload that manages the player's coins: adding, spending, affordability checks, and interest calculations, with a coins_changed signal that drives UI updates. AscensionManager pairs with it to track the player's New Game+ level (0–6) and expose cumulative difficulty modifier dictionaries that scale enemy stats and quota thresholds. Together these two singletons handle all progression-layer state that is not directly run inventory.

tour.title: Tetris Core Engine
tour.description: PieceData, SRS, and BagRandomizer are the three stateless building blocks of the Tetris simulation. PieceData provides SRS-compliant rotation cell offsets and spawn positions for all 7 tetromino types. SRS encodes the official wall-kick tables that govern how pieces rotate near walls and other blocks. BagRandomizer implements the 7-bag piece sequence with seeded-shuffle support, ensuring piece order is reproducible from a given RNG seed. These classes are used exclusively by TetrisBoard.
tour.languageLesson: GDScript static classes (class_name Foo extends RefCounted with only static methods) are equivalent to utility namespaces — they hold no instance state and are called directly as SRS.get_kicks(). This is the idiomatic pattern for pure data and algorithm modules in Godot 4.

tour.title: TetrisBoard: The Simulation Engine
tour.description: TetrisBoard is the core real-time Tetris simulation. It handles all player input (DAS/ARR, soft drop, hard drop, rotation, hold), gravity timing, SRS rotation with wall kicks, T-spin detection, back-to-back and combo tracking, line-clear processing, garbage row insertion, ghost piece rendering, and custom bevel/crack visual effects. When lines are cleared, it constructs an AttackContext and emits an attack signal that RunManager listens to — this is the boundary between the Tetris engine and the roguelite layer.
tour.languageLesson: Godot signals decouple the emitter from its listeners: TetrisBoard emits 'attack' and 'piece_placed' without knowing anything about RunManager or techniques. This keeps the Tetris engine self-contained and testable. The _process and _input callbacks drive the real-time gameplay loop at frame rate.

tour.title: Technique Evaluator
tour.description: TechniqueEvaluator is a pure static evaluator — it takes an AttackContext, a TechniqueRoundState, the player's active technique list, and their keystones, and returns the total bonus damage, economy bonuses, and any side-effect flags for that single attack event. Because it holds no mutable state, it is trivially testable (the unit tests in test_technique_system.gd call it directly) and can be reasoned about in isolation from the rest of the game.

tour.title: RunManager: Game Orchestration
tour.description: RunManager is the largest and most central script in the project (1000+ lines). It is the scene that owns TetrisBoard and wires together every other system: it bootstraps rounds by assembling a RoundConfig from the player's keystones and boss modifiers, listens for TetrisBoard's attack signal and feeds it through TechniqueEvaluator, drives the enemy's garbage timer, handles consumable activation, manages round-win/loss conditions, animates attack popups, and transitions between all game screens. Reading RunManager is like reading the game's main loop.

tour.title: HUD & In-Game Displays
tour.description: The HUD script manages the top bar (round number, timer, coins, boss modifier indicator), the inventory panel showing keystone and technique icons with tween animations, the B2B and combo streak labels, and the backpack consumable slots. EnemyDisplay handles the animated enemy panel (health bar, lunge/pulse/flash animations, name and tier). Together these two scripts show how game state signals from RunManager and RunState are consumed and reflected in the player-facing interface.

tour.title: Between-Round Screens
tour.description: After a round ends, the game flows through a series of transition screens: RoundSuccess shows the payout breakdown and proceed button; KeystoneSelection offers three seeded-random keystone choices filtered by prerequisites; and the Shop lets the player buy and sell techniques, consumables, and vouchers using the Economy and ResourceRegistry singletons. These screens form the roguelite loop — the decision-making layer that wraps every Tetris combat encounter.

tour.title: Save & Persistence Layer
tour.description: RunSave serializes and deserializes the full in-progress run (stage, economy, inventory, RNG seed and state) to user://save.cfg, enabling mid-run save and resume across sessions. ProfileSave persists the player's ascension progress, unlocked item IDs, and lifetime statistics to user://profile.cfg. RunStats is the per-run accumulator (total damage, T-spin damage, highest combo) that feeds both the end-of-run screen and the unlock checker.
tour.languageLesson: Godot's ConfigFile class (used by both RunSave and ProfileSave) stores key-value pairs in INI-style sections and serializes Godot types (Array, Dictionary, Vector2) transparently. This is a lightweight alternative to JSON serialization and handles Godot-native types without manual conversion.

tour.title: Design Specifications
tour.description: The openspec/specs directory holds the authoritative written specifications for every major system — run structure progression, the attack system, techniques, keystones, the economy, and more. These documents were written before or alongside the code and are the source of truth for design intent. When a gameplay formula or rule seems arbitrary, the corresponding spec explains the reasoning. The run-structure spec is especially useful as it defines the 5-ante 4-round progression, quota formulas, and boss assignment logic that RunManager implements.

tour.title: Testing & Export
tour.description: The GUT configuration in .gutconfig.json points the test runner at game/tests/unit/, where each test file exercises a specific system in isolation (technique evaluator, bag randomizer, run state, economy). The export_presets.cfg defines the Windows and Web (HTML5) build targets, both excluding test files, targeting ../builds/, and naming the product Tetrouge. These two config files are the bookends of the development workflow — tests verify correctness, and the export config ships the result.
tour.languageLesson: GUT (Godot Unit Test) test files extend GutTest and use assert_eq, assert_true, and before_each/after_each hooks. Because Godot autoloads persist across test runs, saving and restoring their state in before_each/after_each prevents test bleed-through — a pattern enforced throughout this project's test suite.
